equation_title: the paper's equation with an exponent on each side of each peak
equation_caption: Both add two peaks to a baseline, each a generalized Gaussian with different widths on its left and right. Blue marks what this run's winner does differently: each side of each peak has its own exponent, so a peak can be sharp on one side and shouldered on the other; the second peak sits opposite the first, give or take an offset δ, instead of anywhere; and the curve is clipped at zero. That trades the paper's free second centre for four exponents, 13 parameters in all.
equation_html:
Paper's equation (11 parameters): f(θ) = b + A₁ exp[−½ (|θ−φ₁| / σ₁±)p₁] + A₂ exp[−½ (|θ−φ₂| / σ₂±)p₂]
This run's winner (13 parameters): f(θ) = max{0, b + A₁ exp[−½ (|d₁| / σ₁±)p₁±] + A₂ exp[−½ (|d₂| / σ₂±)p₂±]}, d₁ = θ − φ, d₂ = θ − φ − π − δ
caveats: Twice as long, no better. This run had 24 generations instead of 12, with the same model and settings. Its winner came from generation 15, and on the locked-test neurons it scores 28.331 against 28.322 for the 12-generation winner: a tie within noise. Its held-out error is 0.99% below the double Gaussian's, against 1.01% for the 12-generation winner and 0.84% for the paper's equation.

An exponent from the first generation. As in the 12-generation run, a fitted exponent appeared in generation 0 and in 915 of 942 candidates. The same leakage checks apply (docs/LEAKAGE.md): the model did not know the paper when asked, and its notes credit each term to the plotted neurons.

Peakiness is measured on the sharper side. Each peak has a left and a right exponent; the figures use the lower of the two, which sets the shape of the tip. That makes this winner look peakier than the others: median min(p₁, p₂) 0.66 over all 2,110 reliable neurons, with 30% of locked-test neurons at the floor of 0.5.

α does not match the paper's numbers. The winner gives α ≈ 3.5 (log fit), between the paper's equation refitted here (3.4) and the double Gaussian (4.4). See the 12-generation run's caveat on why the paper's own values are not reproduced.
Different fitter. Candidates are fitted with bounded Levenberg–Marquardt instead of upstream's Adam; scores agree to within about 0.7%.

differences.summary: A baseline plus two asymmetric generalized-Gaussian peaks. The winner gives each side of each peak its own exponent, keeps the second peak within 90° of the opposite direction, and clips the curve at zero.

amplitude A₂ ≥ 0, centred anywhere: opposite φ, shifted by up to ±180°
rows.winner: held within ±90° of the opposite direction
